summary: Forest Service steel tower near Lampe, assembled about 1937-39; a 1992 survey found it in good condition and no longer a lookout. No later source found.

facts.design: Aermotor steel tower, 99.9 ft, observation only, with an enclosed 7 x 7 ft cab

access.note: The 1992 report lists Mo-Ark Water Company, Inc. as present owner and says the site is no longer a fire lookout. It does not describe public access.

events.note: Property on which the site is located purchased (HABS)
Stone County News-Oracle reports construction begun on a 100-foot steel tower to be known as the Wilderness Tower
Tower assembled sometime between 1937 and 1939 by CCC crews from the Shell Knob camp, per a former resident; the 1936 newspaper shows work had begun in 1936
Towerman's dwelling completed by 1940; first towerman's family moved in that year, per a former resident
Annual report for fiscal 1956-57: major repairs made to the residence at Wilderness
Lookout dwelling removed during the early 1960s, basement filled in; now on private land and no longer recognizable as a lookout house
Another building from the dwelling area moved off the site in the early 1960s; now a cow barn on private pasture north of the tower
Annual report for fiscal 1964-65: the Wilderness tower cab was reconditioned
HABS survey: site no longer a fire lookout; tower in good condition apart from missing treads and cab glass; tower likely to be relocated or demolished

corrections.why: The 1992 report says ownership of the land and tower passed from federal to Mo-Ark Water Company, Inc. on September 21, 1992, in a land-for-land exchange, and that the site is no longer a lookout. Check for any later transfer.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1936 newspaper says construction had begun. The 1992 report, citing a former resident, says the tower was assembled between 1937 and 1939 and that the exact date is uncertain. The story gives both; the built event uses 1937, the start of the 1992 range.

notes_for_editor: Today's status is unknown: the newest source is the 1992 HABS report, and no later record was found, so facts.status is left out. The HABS photographs (Library of Congress item MO1226) were not fetched because loc.gov returned 403. The 1939 Crane Chronicle item quoted on the Central US page reports a fatal fall from the tower. It is left out of the story: it is not a fire, and it names a private person. Ownership correction follows the 1992 report; check for any later sale.
